statement: Phase 4 was completed and committed at 1f23dc4. A subsequent audit of the artefacts against the frozen pre-registration found two defects in the analysis code and one unsupported claim in the report text. All three are corrected here. None of them involved retraining, re-running inference, or changing any pre-registered endpoint, contrast, verdict rule or stratum definition: the same saved predictions were re-analysed with the interval procedure the pre-registration actually specified. Every headline verdict is unchanged, and the previous values are recorded below so the correction can be audited rather than taken on trust.
supersedes: the analysis artefacts as committed at 1f23dc4

amendments.found: Blueprint sec.6 and reports/phase4_prereg.json (evaluation.interval_procedure) both require a patient-clustered bootstrap with >=1,000 resamples for every interval. Five analysis scripts used fewer, and the shortfall was not recorded in the deviations list, so every Phase 4 verdict interval as published at 1f23dc4 was computed at below the pre-registered resolution.
amendments.action: all five raised to the pre-registered 1,000 and every affected analysis re-run against the unchanged saved predictions

amendments.found: The RQ3 verdict was read off the arithmetic mean of the three per-seed 95% intervals. That quantity propagates no between-seed variation and has no coverage guarantee, so it should not have been labelled or used as a 95% CI.
amendments.action: the verdict is now read off a pooled patient-clustered bootstrap on the 3-seed mean rho: for each of the 1,000 patient resamples the correlation is computed for all three seeds and averaged, and the percentiles are taken over that distribution. The resamples are shared across seeds because patient_resamples is driven by the fixed pre-registered seed, which is what makes the average paired. The old quantity is retained in the artefact as a descriptive field, explicitly flagged as not a calibrated interval.
amendments.prereg_basis: the frozen verdict rule requires 'a patient-clustered 95% CI excluding 0 on S-majority' and does not prescribe how the three seeds are combined; the pooled interval satisfies that rule, the averaged bounds did not.

amendments.severity: unsupported claim in the report text
amendments.item: the epoch-cap no-bias claim in section 4.6
amendments.found: Section 4.6 stated that the fine-tuning cap 'applies identically to all four new configurations, so it does not bias the contrasts between them'. An identical cap is not identical censoring. The cap bound on 3/3 C2 runs, whose best epochs were at 39, 41 and 41 of 44, against 1/3 for C4; C2 was still improving when it was cut off, and C2 is the treatment arm of the RQ2 primary contrast.
amendments.action: the claim is withdrawn. Section 4.6 now reports the per-arm cap incidence and best-epoch positions, states that the censoring is asymmetric, names the direction of the resulting bias as running against C2 and towards the NOT RESOLVED verdict that was obtained, and qualifies that verdict as 'not resolved under this compute budget'. Appendix B's note is aligned with it.
amendments.not_corrected_by_this_amendment: the censoring itself. Removing it requires letting every arm early-stop on its own, which is a retraining amendment (Phase 4B) that must be declared before it is run and reported separately from the pre-registered primary.

verdict_comparison.note: every pre-registered verdict is unchanged. Point estimates are identical because they are plug-in statistics that do not depend on the resample count; only the interval endpoints move.

outstanding.item: statistical power on the RQ2 primary endpoint
outstanding.status: NOT fixed by this amendment, and not fixable by re-analysis
outstanding.detail: the pooled contested stratum is 550 images clustered within patients, and no precision or power statement was pre-registered. The realised half-width on C2-C3 cannot resolve an effect of the size observed. Phase 5 should pre-register a target precision.

see P4-AMD-3; requires the Phase 4B retraining amendment, which was costed and deliberately not run. Cost: 6 full runs from scratch, about 17 h at 70 fine-tuning epochs. It is NOT resumable from the existing checkpoints -- phase4_train.py builds the cosine schedule with T_max equal to the cap (cosine_T=max_ft), so raising the cap changes the learning-rate curve across the entire fine-tuning phase and the capped runs are not a prefix of uncapped ones. An earlier estimate of ~5 h in this project assumed incremental epochs on resumed runs and was wrong.
